extracted.intended_audience: Nonprofit organizations, advocacy groups, researchers, community groups, and other potential grantees seeking funding from the Hewlett Foundation Environment program.
extracted.subtask_description: Program-level guidance for organizations seeking grants from the Hewlett Foundation's Environment program, describing priority themes, strategy emphases, geographic focus, and desired partnership types for grant proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance climate change actions that help reduce emissions, create jobs, and ensure all benefit from the clean energy economy.
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance climate change actions that help reduce emissions, create jobs, and ensure all benefit from the clean energy economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hewlett views climate change as an interconnected challenge and seeks ways for all to benefit from a clean energy future. The Foundation supports efforts that bring government, private industry, and communities together to reduce emissions, with attention to improving community well‑being and safeguarding a flourishing planet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bolster efforts that bring nations together to identify shared climate solutions that help everyone thrive.
rubrics_metrics.description: Bolster efforts that bring nations together, despite their differences, to identify shared climate solutions that help everyone thrive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support includes backing grantees that work on international collaboration and multilateral approaches so countries can find common ground on climate action and shared solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve landscapes and waterways in Western United States for the health and well-being of people and wildlife.
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve landscapes and waterways in Western United States for the health and well-being of people and wildlife.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Western Conservation strategy focuses on conserving lands and waters of the U.S. West to benefit both people and wildlife, emphasizing long‑term stewardship and community health. The Foundation has funded this work since 1969 and prioritizes projects that contribute to these outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic emphasis on key contributors and regions: U.S., Europe, China, and India.
rubrics_metrics.description: We pay particular attention to the U.S., Europe, China, and India, key contributors to global emissions and emerging solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that address emissions and solutions in these geographies, or that engage with actors from these regions, align with the program's strategic focus. Geographic relevance is an explicit strategic consideration for climate-related grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support grantees partnering with multilateral institutions and cross-sector actors.
rubrics_metrics.description: We also support grantees partnering with multilateral institutions to help countries find common ground on climate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program favors initiatives that leverage multilateral bodies and that convene or coordinate across government, private sector, and community stakeholders to achieve scalable and cooperative climate outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage a broad, diverse set of local partners and build partnerships based on trust and respect.
rubrics_metrics.description: We engage with a broad range of grantee partners including Tribes, ranchers and landowners, hunters and anglers, conservation advocates, faith leaders, and scientists, and build partnerships based on trust and respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful conservation work should involve diverse constituencies and emphasize relationship‑building. Proposals that demonstrate inclusive engagement and trust-based partnership practices are aligned with the Foundation's Western Conservation approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work across differences and across levels (local, state, national) to find long-term solutions.
rubrics_metrics.description: When people work across difference, at the local, state, and national levels, they can find solutions to the interconnected challenges to the health of their communities, public and private lands, wildlife, and waterways — for the long term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is given to efforts that facilitate cross-level collaboration and durable solutions addressing interconnected environmental and community well‑being challenges. Emphasis on long-term impact rather than short-term fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity and community well-being as explicit outcomes of climate and conservation work.
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to improve community well‑being and safeguard a flourishing planet; ensure all benefit from a clean energy economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should articulate how interventions will create equitable benefits (e.g., jobs, improved local conditions) and contribute to broader community health and resilience, not only emissions reductions or habitat protection.
